nginx.purpose: Serve static sites or put a reverse proxy in front of a local application.
nginx.configuration: /etc/nginx/; site definitions usually live in sites-available/ and sites-enabled/.
nginx.notes: Validate configuration before reloading. Do not expose an unfinished application to the internet.

lighttpd.purpose: Serve websites with a compact HTTP server.
lighttpd.notes: Another HTTP server may already own port 80. Run one listener per address and port.

apache.purpose: Host websites with Apache HTTP Server and its module ecosystem.
apache.configuration: /etc/apache2/; sites-available/ and sites-enabled/ contain virtual-host definitions.
apache.notes: Check for port conflicts with Nginx, Caddy, or Lighttpd before starting another web server.

caddy.purpose: Run an HTTP server or reverse proxy with a concise Caddyfile.
caddy.notes: Automatic public certificates require a suitable domain, DNS, and network reachability. Installation alone does not provide a domain or configure your proxy.

mariadb.purpose: Store relational application data in a MySQL-compatible database.
mariadb.notes: Create a separate database and least-privilege user for each application. Use database-aware dumps or snapshots; a copy of live data files is not a reliable logical backup.

postgres.purpose: Run PostgreSQL for applications that need a relational SQL database.
postgres.configuration: /etc/postgresql/ and /var/lib/postgresql/; the package determines the installed major version.
postgres.notes: Configure pg_hba.conf deliberately and avoid making the database publicly reachable. Use pg_dump or a suitable database backup strategy.

redis.purpose: Provide an in-memory cache or application data store.
redis.notes: Do not expose an unauthenticated Redis listener. A cache is not automatically a durable primary database.

memcached.purpose: Provide a disposable in-memory cache for supported applications.
memcached.notes: Keep the listener on a trusted interface. Cache contents can disappear on restart; do not treat them as a backup.

docker.purpose: Run containerized services with Debian-packaged Docker Engine and Compose.
docker.configuration: /etc/docker/ and /var/lib/docker/; Compose project files belong with each project.
docker.notes: The recipe adds the invoking sudo user to the docker group. That group grants powerful host access; log out and back in for group changes. This recipe installs docker-compose, so do not assume the newer docker compose plugin exists.

podman.purpose: Run OCI containers with Podman, including rootless workflows where supported.
podman.configuration: User containers use per-user storage; root-run containers use separate system storage.
podman.notes: Rootless operation can need subordinate UID/GID ranges and extra packages. An installed engine is not a configured application stack.

samba.purpose: Share selected directories with Windows and other SMB clients.
samba.notes: Create shares and Samba users explicitly. Match Unix permissions to the intended access; enabling smbd does not create a safe public share.

nfs.purpose: Export filesystem paths to trusted Linux or Unix clients.
nfs.notes: Restrict exports to intended clients and preserve appropriate root-squash behavior. Do not expose an NFS export directly to the internet.

syncthing.purpose: Synchronize selected folders between devices using peer-to-peer file synchronization.
syncthing.configuration: Per-user Syncthing configuration and state; exact paths follow the packaged version.
syncthing.notes: Replace YOUR_USER in the example. Review folder sharing, remote device IDs, and GUI access. Synchronization can propagate deletion; keep independent backups.

cockpit.purpose: Manage the machine through the Cockpit web console.
cockpit.configuration: The package uses socket activation; review Cockpit and system authentication settings.
cockpit.notes: The catalog enables cockpit.socket; the usual web port is 9090. Keep management access on a trusted network and review authentication before opening firewall rules.

prometheus-node.purpose: Expose host metrics for a Prometheus monitoring server.
prometheus-node.configuration: Debian service defaults and command-line flags determine enabled collectors and listen address.
prometheus-node.notes: Node exporter supplies metrics; it does not install a Prometheus database or Grafana dashboard. Limit access to monitoring clients.

gitea-light.purpose: This legacy recipe targets Gogs, a lightweight Git hosting service; it does not install Gitea.
gitea-light.configuration: Gogs configuration depends on the package source and deployment method.
gitea-light.notes: Availability-sensitive recipe: it requests the gogs package and service. Verify apt-cache policy first; if no candidate exists, this recipe cannot install it from your configured repositories. No alternate repository is added by this recipe.

mosquitto.purpose: Run an MQTT message broker for local automation and IoT projects.
mosquitto.notes: Define listeners and authentication before sharing access. mosquitto_sub and mosquitto_pub are supplied by mosquitto-clients; use a test topic on your own broker.

gitdaemon.purpose: A legacy recipe intended to support serving Git repositories over the git protocol.
gitdaemon.configuration: The current recipe requests the packages git and daemon but adds no managed service or repository export configuration.
gitdaemon.notes: The daemon package is not the same thing as configuring git daemon. Read the installed Git help and configure a deliberate service before use. The git protocol does not provide SSH authentication.

python.purpose: Develop Python applications in isolated virtual environments.
python.configuration: Keep a virtual environment and dependency lock or requirements file with each project.
python.notes: Use a venv for application dependencies. Avoid installing arbitrary pip packages into the OS-managed Python environment.

pipx.purpose: Install Python command-line applications into separate managed virtual environments.
pipx.configuration: Per-user pipx directories and shell PATH configuration.
pipx.notes: Run pipx as your regular user. The recipe runs ensurepath for the sudo-invoking user, but a new login may be required.

nodejs.purpose: Develop JavaScript applications with Debian-packaged Node.js and npm.
nodejs.configuration: package.json and your lockfile live in the project directory.
nodejs.notes: The Debian version can differ from upstream current releases. Check your project engine requirements; do not assume a specific major version from this recipe.

java.purpose: Compile and run Java code with the default Debian OpenJDK toolchain.
java.configuration: Project build files determine dependencies; JAVA_HOME may be needed by some tools.
java.notes: The catalog targets the Debian bookworm default JDK, documented as OpenJDK 17. Verify the installed version against the application requirement.

go.purpose: Compile Go applications with the Debian Go toolchain.
go.configuration: Use go.mod and go.sum in each module.
go.notes: Verify the compiler version before building a module that requires a newer Go release.

rust.purpose: Compile Rust applications with Debian-packaged rustc and Cargo.
rust.configuration: Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock live with each project.
rust.notes: This recipe does not install rustup. Debian package versions can be older than a project minimum supported Rust version.

php.purpose: Run PHP applications through PHP-FPM or the PHP command line.
php.configuration: /etc/php/; pool configuration is under the installed version fpm/pool.d/ directory.
php.notes: The post-install hook targets php8.2-fpm for bookworm. A web server must be configured separately to pass PHP requests to FPM.

ruby.purpose: Run Ruby scripts and develop Ruby applications.
ruby.configuration: Project Gemfile and lockfile; per-project dependency management is recommended.
ruby.notes: Installing Ruby does not install an application server or configure a Rails deployment.

perl-dev.purpose: Add module-build support to the base Perl environment.
perl-dev.configuration: Use the project build files and distribution-specific Perl module packages.
perl-dev.notes: This entry adds libmodule-build-perl, rather than a separate full Perl development distribution.

build-essential.purpose: Compile native software with GCC, Make, and pkg-config support.
build-essential.configuration: Each source project supplies its own build configuration.
build-essential.notes: Compiler tools do not make downloaded source trustworthy. Use a non-root build directory and inspect install steps.

code-help.purpose: Add fuzzy finding and syntax-highlighted file viewing through fzf and bat.
code-help.configuration: Shell integration is optional and follows your shell configuration.
code-help.notes: Although the legacy display name mentions exa, the recipe installs only fzf and bat. On Debian the bat command is commonly named batcat.

wireguard.purpose: Install WireGuard userspace tools for a configured VPN tunnel.
wireguard.configuration: /etc/wireguard/ for configurations you create; protect private keys.
wireguard.notes: The recipe installs tools, not a ready-made VPN or keypair. Define peers, routes, and firewall rules before bringing a tunnel up.

openvpn.purpose: Use OpenVPN with an independently supplied client or server configuration.
openvpn.notes: Certificates, keys, and configuration are not generated by this recipe. Protect credentials and review routed networks before connecting.

tailscale.purpose: Install the Tailscale mesh-VPN client through its upstream installer.
tailscale.configuration: Tailscale authentication and node access rules are configured separately.
tailscale.notes: The recipe downloads and runs an upstream shell installer. Inspect its source before use. Installing does not automatically authenticate the machine or grant tailnet access.

mosh.purpose: Use a roaming terminal connection that tolerates changing network conditions.
mosh.configuration: SSH access bootstraps the session; Mosh also needs permitted UDP connectivity.
mosh.notes: Install the client on the connecting machine too. Confirm remote access and network policy before relying on Mosh.

nmap.purpose: Inspect hosts and services on networks you own or have permission to test.
nmap.configuration: Command-line scan options define scope; start with localhost.
nmap.notes: Use an explicit authorized target. Network scanning may be disruptive on fragile devices; avoid broad unknown networks.

tshark.purpose: Analyze network traffic with the Wireshark command-line interface.
tshark.configuration: Capture permissions and interfaces determine what a regular user can inspect.
tshark.notes: Packet captures can contain credentials or private traffic. Capture only what you are authorized to inspect and protect the resulting files.

tcpdump.purpose: Capture and inspect packets for network troubleshooting.
tcpdump.configuration: Choose an explicit interface and filter; save captures outside public directories.
tcpdump.notes: Captures can contain sensitive data. Keep capture scope small and avoid publishing unreviewed capture files.

fail2ban.purpose: Apply log-driven bans for repeated unwanted authentication attempts.
fail2ban.notes: Review enabled jails and their log sources. Fail2ban complements working authentication and firewall rules; installation is not complete security hardening.

ufw.purpose: Manage host firewall rules with a straightforward command-line frontend.
ufw.configuration: Use ufw commands to define rules; do not assume the firewall is active after package installation.
ufw.notes: If you connect remotely, allow your actual SSH port before enabling or tightening the firewall. Keep a recovery console available.

auditd.purpose: Record kernel audit events for system investigation and policy monitoring.
auditd.notes: Review retention and disk use. An installed audit daemon does not provide a tailored audit ruleset.

clamav.purpose: Scan files with an open-source antivirus engine.
clamav.configuration: /etc/clamav/; signatures must be updated before meaningful scanning.
clamav.notes: Engine and signatures both matter. This recipe does not configure an automatic schedule or promise detection of every threat.

rkhunter.purpose: Run heuristic checks for rootkit indicators and suspicious system changes.
rkhunter.notes: Investigate findings rather than treating every warning as proof of compromise. Create baselines only on a system you trust.

unattended.purpose: Provide automated package-upgrade tooling for supported repositories.
unattended.configuration: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/; inspect allowed origins and periodic APT settings.
unattended.notes: A running service alone does not prove scheduled updates are enabled correctly. Review timers, origins, reboot behavior, and logs.

btop.purpose: Inspect CPU, memory, disks, processes, and network activity interactively.
btop.notes: This is an interactive local monitor; it does not retain a historical metrics database.

htop.purpose: Inspect and manage running processes from a terminal.
htop.notes: htop is also listed in the base image packages; this recipe can ensure it is installed. Stopping processes can interrupt services.

tmux.purpose: Keep terminal sessions running and split a terminal into panes.
tmux.notes: Default detach keys are Ctrl+B then D. Reconnect with tmux attach -t work; sessions still end when the machine reboots.

screen.purpose: Keep a terminal session alive across a disconnected SSH connection.
screen.notes: Default detach keys are Ctrl+A then D. Reattach with screen -r work.

byobu.purpose: Add a terminal session interface around tmux or screen.
byobu.configuration: Per-user Byobu configuration and selected backend.
byobu.notes: Keyboard shortcuts depend on backend and terminal. Review the built-in help before changing a remote session layout.

mc.purpose: Browse and manage files in a two-panel terminal interface.
mc.notes: File deletion and moves act on the actual filesystem. Use your regular user unless administration explicitly requires root.

ncdu.purpose: Find directories consuming disk space with an interactive disk-usage browser.
ncdu.configuration: The path passed to ncdu determines the scan root.
ncdu.notes: The -x option stays on one filesystem. Deletion actions remove real data; inspect before deleting.

neofetch.purpose: Show a terminal summary of the OS and hardware.
neofetch.notes: System summaries can expose hostnames or hardware details. Review output before sharing it publicly.

fastfetch-lite.purpose: Inspect system and hardware information with inxi.
fastfetch-lite.configuration: inxi command options determine detail and privacy filtering.
fastfetch-lite.notes: Despite its legacy ID, this recipe installs inxi, not Fastfetch. Check output for identifiers before posting a support report.

tree.purpose: Print a directory hierarchy from the terminal.
tree.configuration: Choose a directory and depth with command-line flags.
tree.notes: Filenames can contain private information. Limit depth when making a report.

tldr.purpose: Read concise command examples using a tldr client.
tldr.configuration: Client cache and page update settings follow the packaged implementation.
tldr.notes: Command examples are a starting point, not a substitute for understanding destructive flags. Manual pages are stripped from the minimal image by default.

iperf3.purpose: Measure network throughput between a client and a server you control.
iperf3.configuration: Run a test server and client deliberately; the recipe does not configure a continuous measurement service.
iperf3.notes: Throughput testing can saturate a link. Coordinate the test and restrict access to a server you intentionally start.

smartmontools.purpose: Inspect drive SMART information and hardware health.
smartmontools.notes: Health reports are not backups or guarantees against drive failure. Device and adapter support varies.

lm-sensors.purpose: Read supported hardware temperature, voltage, and fan sensors.
lm-sensors.configuration: Hardware detection and module configuration depend on the motherboard.
lm-sensors.notes: The recipe invokes sensors-detect --auto; this probes hardware and may need a reboot or modules loaded. No sensor or fan-control support is guaranteed.

nvme.purpose: Inspect and administer NVMe storage devices with nvme-cli.
nvme.configuration: Commands target explicit NVMe controller or namespace devices.
nvme.notes: Administrative NVMe commands can erase data or change firmware. Start with read-only inspection and keep backups.

rsync-server.purpose: Copy files efficiently locally or over SSH with rsync.
rsync-server.configuration: Replace SOURCE and DESTINATION with your paths; the trailing slash affects copy semantics.
rsync-server.notes: The example is a dry run. The recipe installs rsync but does not configure a public rsync daemon; --delete can remove destination files.

git.purpose: Track source code history and work with remote repositories.
git.configuration: Per-project .git directories and user-level Git configuration.
git.notes: Set an appropriate author identity before committing. Review staged changes and never commit credentials.

xfce.purpose: Add a full XFCE desktop and LightDM to the minimal OS.
xfce.configuration: LightDM and desktop session settings; additional disk and memory are required.
xfce.notes: The recipe sets graphical.target as the default boot target. Reboot when ready. To return to text boot, use sudo systemctl set-default multi-user.target and reboot; this does not uninstall the desktop.

lxde.purpose: Add a lightweight LXDE desktop and LightDM.
lxde.configuration: LightDM and LXDE session settings; image size grows after installation.
lxde.notes: The recipe sets graphical.target. Hardware graphics support still depends on the kernel and installed drivers. To return to text boot, set multi-user.target and reboot.
